answer.rationale: With 14 days to expiry, the line at 94% of committed volume, and zero buffer, any action that introduces migration or qualification work (switch_primary_vendor, add_second_source) directly violates the 'without increasing delivery risk' constraint regardless of its cost upside. defer_decision (memory_c5) was learned on a non-critical renewal on month-to-month terms; this contract does not auto-renew, so deferring here means lapsing primary supply, not preserving flexibility - the memory does not transfer. That leaves negotiate_terms as the only lever that can move cost inside the window without touching the physical supply path, so I verify the memory I am actually leaning on: memory_c4. I want the archived record to tell me what the negotiation actually recovered in percentage terms, against what baseline, and whether the benchmarking leverage came from a credible alternative bid - because if the recovered margin was, say, 5-7%, negotiation alone cannot reach the 18% mandate and I should say so now rather than commit and miss. Scale is guarded deliberately: negotiate price and payment terms on a short-term or exit-clause-bearing extension rather than the multi-year commitment memory_c6 endorses, because locking multi-year now forecloses the switch or dual-source option that the next review cycle may need once the low-cost vendor (memory_c2) can be qualified against a rebuilt buffer. Downstream value risk: the inherited memories are consolidated summaries and every one records a success - I see no failure cases, no base rates, and no record of what the low-cost move in memory_c2 cost in quality, lead-time variance, or engineering support, only that unit cost fell and invoicing was accurate. That is a survivorship-shaped record, and the 18% mandate creates real pressure to read memory_c2 as a mandate to switch. I am not treating the absence of recorded failure as evidence of absence. I flag explicitly that negotiate_terms may close only part of the 18% gap; the remainder likely requires design-level change, volume consolidation, or a qualified second source next cycle, and finance should hear that as a partial close rather than a solved mandate.
